items.check: **No workarounds**: No TODOs, FIXMEs, stubs, or partially-implemented features
items.evidence: Both native rejection/cleanup roots and the Qore declaration view are corrected directly. Strict validation remains strict; optional reset assertions are phase-specific. Existing upstream comments in exact replacement context are not new stubs.

items.check: **Exception safety**: C++ uses `ReferenceHolder` for Qore allocations, `std::unique_ptr` for C++ allocations, `*xsink` checked after every fallible operation
items.evidence: Native change introduces no allocation or ownership transfer. Schema cleanup retains whole annotation subtrees; the allocation harness checks 131 faults through private/public paths, baseline live counts and recovery. All affected Valgrind runs have zero errors/lost blocks.

items.check: **Thread safety**: All mutable shared state protected by `std::lock_guard<std::mutex>` or documented as immutable-after-construction
items.evidence: No shared production state added. Native validation contexts remain per call, namespace maps are local copy-on-write values, and concurrent reader/provider/HTTP regressions pass.

items.check: **Type safety**: Strongly-typed `code<return(args)>` instead of untyped `code`; `static_cast` instead of C casts; typed hashdecls for results; enums where appropriate
items.evidence: Qore conversion uses typed references and namespace maps; schema text is type-checked. Allocation phases use an enum; C test records and native schema pointers retain concrete types.

items.check: **Performance**: No O(n²) where O(n) is possible; no unnecessary copies; coordinate descent uses incremental residuals not full matrix multiply
items.evidence: Source normalization retains conditional suffix merging and reference traversal. Whitespace is scanned once; native cleanup skips annotation subtrees. No additional traversal, numeric expansion or global cache is introduced.

items.check: **Error handling**: All inputs validated (dimensions, empty data, unfitted models); C++ I/O handles EAGAIN/EINTR if applicable
items.evidence: Significant declaration text, non-XML whitespace, unbound/unknown types, invalid facets/content/attributes, abstract types and forbidden namespaces reject with the required API errors. Failed schema additions and validation recovery are tested.

items.check: **Documentation**: Doxygen `@param`, `@return`, `@throw` on all public methods; `@par Example` with realistic business scenarios; `@note` for important caveats
items.evidence: No new public API. WSDL/native release notes, README, durable designs, allocation-phase explanation and an executed shipment example document the behavior and diagnostic boundaries; qdx/Doxygen are clean.

items.check: **QPP flags**: `[flags=CONSTANT]` on methods that never throw; `[flags=RET_VALUE_ONLY]` on methods that throw but have no side effects
items.evidence: No QPP class, native public method or method flags changed.

items.check: **Security**: No user-controlled format strings; no buffer overflows; bounds checking on array indices; no credentials in code
items.evidence: Only static test templates are format strings, snprintf results are bounded, source hashes are checked before applying fixes, and no credentials or new resource access are introduced.

items.check: **Correctness**: Algorithms verified against reference implementations; edge cases tested (empty data, single sample, all-zero features)
items.evidence: All 130 suites, 27 mode/AOT/matrix/consumer supplements, 43 provider tests, independent 684-document and 96-schema matrices, Valgrind, documentation and unchanged both-version corpus outcomes pass. Original invalid inputs and validator disagreements remain explicit.
